about: What a wikilink target names (M55.8, M60.9). A name resolves in four passes: filename stem, then the folder of a project.md, then an item key, then exact title, all case-insensitive and trimmed, each pass taking the first entry in order; an empty name resolves nothing. An item key is an entry's key property when it is a string shaped PREFIX-N after an ASCII trim: one or more ASCII letter-or-digit segments joined by -, then - and ASCII digits (FLD-13, MY-TEAM-12). A project's own key: FLD, any other shape, and a number are no key. An entry's optional key here becomes its properties.key in both replayers. A target is read whole first. Only when that names nothing and the target holds a #, the text before its FIRST # is resolved as the page, and the text after it, trimmed, is the section (none when empty). So nothing that resolved before section links changes, and a title that holds a # stays a title link. The fragment is never cut from the file or from outgoingLinks. Replayed by replays_the_shared_target_cases in src-tauri/src/vault/link.rs, which checks path only, and by src/engine/wikilink.test.ts, which checks path and section. `why` is for the reader.

cases.why: A project is reached by its folder, and the folder outranks a page titled Atlas.
The page before the #, the heading after it.
Both halves are trimmed.
The page half runs the folder pass like any name.
The page half runs the title pass like any name.
The whole target goes first, so a title that holds a # stays a title link.
An empty section is none: the link reaches the page.
Only the first # splits.
No page half: it names a section of the page the link sits in, which only that page can answer.
A page half that names nothing dangles.
Case never decides the stem.
Resolves to the page; the editor lands only on headings.
No stem, folder or title answers, so the item key does.
Case never decides the key.
The name is trimmed before the key pass.
The page half runs the key pass like any name.
A prefix may hold dashes; only the tail must be a number.
A stem beats a key.
A project folder beats a key.
A key beats a title, even one earlier in order: the only target the key pass moved.
A project's own key is a prefix, not an item key.
A key with no -number tail is no key.
A number is no key.
Two entries share a key: the earlier one wins.
